title: What Happens If You Swallow Chewing Gum?
sources: Cleveland Clinic Health Essentials, 'What Happens When You Swallow Gum?' (gum base is 'largely synthetic'; 'Gum base isn't able to be digested, so it just stays in your guts all the way through and doesn't break down'; 'it'll come out about 40 hours later in your stool'; 'Gum doesn't stay in your stomach for seven years or even seven days'; 'Swallowing one piece of gum probably won't hurt you'; swallowing it every day or a 'mega-wad' of four pieces 'can cause an intestinal blockage'; seek care for blockage symptoms such as abdominal pain, constipation, cramping, vomiting): https://health.clevelandclinic.org/what-happens-when-you-swallow-gum/

Duke Health blog, 'Myth or Fact: It Takes Seven Years to Digest Chewing Gum' ('Our bodies do not possess digestive enzymes to specifically break down gum base'; gum passes through like food and leaves in stool; the doctor, who has reviewed upper endoscopies in children and adults: 'I have yet to see a wad of gum lying around in the stomach'): https://dukehealth.org/blog/myth-or-fact-it-takes-seven-years-digest-chewing-gum

Milov DE et al., 'Chewing gum bezoars of the gastrointestinal tract', Pediatrics 1998;102(2):e22 (three children with gut or esophageal blockage after regularly swallowing gum): https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/9685468/

Tease (next video): Cleveland Clinic, 'Eye Twitching' (muscles in or near your eye move without you controlling them; usually harmless; the most common type, myokymia, is most often in the lower eyelid): https://my.clevelandclinic.org/health/symptoms/17663-eye-twitching

lines.text: What happens if you swallow chewing gum?
Seven years inside you, or gone in days? Guess.
Gulp. Gum base is mostly synthetic. No enzyme in you breaks it.
lines.caps: *GULP | GUM *BASE | IS MOSTLY *SYNTHETIC | NO *ENZYME IN YOU | *BREAKS IT

lines.text: It stays whole the entire trip, never breaking down.
Ever gulped yours mid-meeting and heard a parent's warning?
But here's the twist: whole doesn't mean stuck.
It doesn't cling. It rides along with food.
A Duke doctor reviewing stomach scopes hasn't seen one gum wad.
lines.caps: A *DUKE DOCTOR | REVIEWING STOMACH *SCOPES | HASN'T *SEEN | ONE *GUM WAD

lines.text: It's B: out in your poop, about forty hours later.
lines.caps: IT'S *B: OUT | IN YOUR *POOP | ABOUT *40 HOURS | *LATER

lines.text: Rare exception: blockages, mostly kids swallowing lots of gum daily.
Next Body File: eyelid twitches that won't quit, mostly the lower lid.
